translations.answer: The project contributor explicitly stated that [0,-1,0] is the Coriolis/Centrifugal effect, which can be calculated separately using pin.computeCoriolisMatrix(model, data, q, qd) @ qd. The free-flyer configuration should not be all-zero; using pin.neutral(model) ensures normalization of the quaternion. The contributor's use of the neutral configuration still reproduces the same cross-term, indicating it is not solely caused by a full-zero q. The original post did not respond to the question about whether the cross-term disappears after replacing q=0 with the neutral configuration. The answer is therefore a partial explanation.
translations.applicability: Applicable to the minimal model of a humanoid robot in the Pinocchio free-flyer context, where speed-related RNEA bias terms are identified. Version not specified; specific human-like model needs independent verification.
translations.credibility.rationale: There is engineering record for the environment, processing steps, and results, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The original author used three sets of qd outputs to identify the bias term, and an additional rotational degree of freedom model was used for supplementary comparison.
translations.details.attempts.1: The project contributor replaced q=0 in the original code with pin.neutral(model), and reproduced the same y=-1 output.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: The project contributor stated that the [0,-1,0] can be calculated separately using pin.computeCoriolisMatrix(model, data, q, qd) @ qd, and compared with the RNEA extra term.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Using pin.neutral(model) to initialize the free-flyer configuration prevents full-zero quaternions from being unnormalized.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: This is not a numerical error to be deleted; the term is identified as Coriolis/centrifugal speed bias, and pin.neutral(model) is used to initialize the valid free-flyer configuration.
translations.details.environments.0: Pinocchio Python API, buildModelFromUrdf(..., JointModelFreeFlyer()), 1 kg point mass model; version, operating system, and hardware not specified.
translations.details.limits.0: The original author did not respond to whether the computeCoriolisMatrix @ qd is consistent with this term.
translations.details.limits.1: Why does the additional rotational joint model no longer produce the same cross-term? The thread does not provide an explanation, and this is not inferred.
translations.details.limits.2: The thread does not state the Pinocchio version, and does not extend the minimal example to specific humanoid robot WBC values.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The project contributor provided a classification of the cross-term and a path for separate calculation, and used the neutral configuration to reproduce the original output.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does RNEA return a y=-1 force when the free flyer has both z-direction linear velocity and x-direction angular velocity?
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The project contributor explicitly stated that [0,-1,0] is the Coriolis/Centrifugal effect.
translations.details.symptoms.0: When qd=[0,0,1,1,0,0] and qdd=0, RNEA returns [0,-1,9.81,0,0,0]; no y=-1 term is present when there is no speed or only z-direction linear velocity.
translations.details.symptoms.1: When the x-direction angular velocity is replaced with an additional rotational joint speed, the cross-term disappears in the original author's supplementary example.
